bridgeRouteRisk.summary: nOPAL has four reviewed independent native-issuance routes on Ethereum, Plume, BSC, and Plasma; the Plume, BSC, and Plasma rows retain Ethereum as the issuer's primary reference but are canonical native issuance, not peripheral bridge representations. Nest's current registry and nOPAL integration guide identify a Solana LayerZero OFT route via OFT store FmeHf1FQJhXUWHVfLACCHJ8KvAJ7jpiDvukz8ZHP7XLq, authored below alongside two further LayerZero OFT representations established by fresh on-chain reads on 2026-09-05: the World Chain NestShareOFT proxy and the Avalanche deployment whose implementation bytecode is byte-identical to the verified World Chain NestShareOFT implementation apart from the per-chain LayerZero endpoint constant. The Plasma native deployment is live per the issuer registry but dormant, with zero supply at the reviewed block. The peripheral OFT controller identities and proxy/program upgrade authority paths were verified at fixed blocks on 2026-09-05; complete LayerZero peer/DVN configuration, controller signer topology, limits and recovery remain unverified.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex bridge route review; Kimi P2 control cohort dc-7 (lead pyusd-paypal); FIX2-09 Mint/Bridge boundary migration 2026-08-16; U5 Nest rail closeout 2026-09-05

routes.reviewNote: Independent native nOPAL issuance on Plasma, not a bridge representation. At Plasma block 31652535 on 2026-09-05, name() was 'Nest BlackOpal LiquidStone II Vault', symbol() nOPAL, decimals() 6, totalSupply() 0, and owner() is the Nest Timelock 0x8faacdc65de5d78975df4f9dc4b6548979ceb23a, the same owner as the Ethereum, Plume, and BSC deployments. The contract is a direct non-proxy deployment whose runtime bytecode is byte-for-byte the Ethereum nOPAL share contract except chain-specific immutables around the chain-id constant, and it contains no LayerZero endpoint, lzReceive, or peer surfaces. The deployment is live per Nest's registry (plasma startBlock 4904024) but dormant, with zero supply at the reviewed block.

routes.reviewNote: At worldchain block 34645982 (2026-09-05T17:00:03.000Z, hash 0x07a5129b27fca11df9e8a4a73d001992a673e01e540e7f53e8c431d9757db487), the exact NestShareOFT proxy owner() returned 0x8faacdc65de5d78975df4f9dc4b6548979ceb23a; EIP-1967 slots identify implementation 0x9c0ea3cdfed77032fcfa07e9cbd3628a9c5c39bb and ProxyAdmin 0x4ac70c01c8a7fa4984c50fe8a503dd70ba7c6cb2, whose owner() returned the same controller. Proxy, implementation, ProxyAdmin and controller code are nonempty. Read-only eth_call simulations from that controller succeed for setPeer(30101, existing peer) and ProxyAdmin.upgradeAndCall(proxy, current implementation, 0x); both reject unrelated address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001 with OwnableUnauthorizedAccount. This proves distinct OFT-owner and proxy-upgrade authority paths, not controller signer topology or effective delay: getMinDelay() returns 172800 seconds, but proposer/executor roles and bypasses were not inventoried. Controller identity is recorded conservatively as a contract. Complete peer/DVN configuration, limits, custody and recovery remain unverified. Implementation code hex-text SHA-256 9cad6178eb3db3c314e7539c0b1dbd2ed7b20cfebb42eaa6a195201e3c345567; raw block/read/simulation export SHA-256 389ad4220296f7e430aafb6db990a1b484a8cff3dc874f4b53f4ab671cf5b907. Deployed implementation bytecode exactly matches the explorer verified-source record.
